recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only as part of broader search-prefix semantics review; FHIR-7957 itself is already reflected in the current source.
issue_request: FHIR-7957 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the DSTU1 search page. It asked to avoid symbolic date comparison prefixes and the final resolution was to use two-character operator combinations, with eq assumed when no operator is present.
initial_application: Jira records application as svn revision 5816. No current Git commit message in this checkout directly mentions FHIR-7957, but the active search source and later refactors preserve the prefix-code approach rather than the old >, >=, <=, and < wording.
additional_context: 2015-07-08 FHIR Infrastructure minutes record agreement with Lloyd's proposed resolution for #7957. Later published issue FHIR-10797 is in the same date-search family and cites 7938/7957 while reinforcing the ge/le date-range pattern.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/search.html defines the prefix codes eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, sa, eb, and ap; says eq is assumed when no prefix is present; and shows a date range using ge/le.

related_jiras.note: Later Published date-range clarification explicitly references 7938/7957 and confirms ge/le date range examples.
Earlier Resolved-No-Change discussion shows alternative symbolic or pathed prefix syntaxes were considered but not adopted.
